incident-bot: ALERT: Eval gate 'safety_v2' fired for workspace=acme-corp, run=2026-03-14T09:45:19Z. Trigger=output_drift (safety_score drop > 10%) · pager: https://pagerduty.com/ABCDE12345 :rotating_light:
PagerDuty: New incident PDR-98321 opened and notifying on-call. Priority: P2. Link: https://pagerduty.com/incidents/PDR-98321
Alice Hart: acked PDR-98321 — I'm on it, switching to incident channel. Anyone on-call for dedicated infra?
Ben Kapoor: oncall here. seeing a spike in 'unsafe' labels for prompts that previously passed. Rate is ~12% failing vs baseline 1.1%.
Cheng Li: chiming in — looks like a model rollout finished ~09:42 UTC to v3.1-quant. Eval gateway started getting higher toxicity scores at ~09:44. Could be model change or eval config drift.
Dave Morales: customer-facing: Acme reported 5 users seeing truncated or redacted outputs; support ticket #65902. They say it's blocking a demo.
Eve Sinclair: quick ask — can we temporarily disable the eval-gate for acme-corp to stop pages and avoid noisy escalations while we triage?
Alice Hart: prefer not to fully disable. Proposal: route acme-corp traffic to fallback model variant (v3.0-stable) and set eval-gate to mute-only (no page) for that workspace. That buys time. Anyone comfortable performing rollout?
Ben Kapoor: I can push traffic reroute. Command: 
```
redwood route update --workspace acme-corp --model v3.0-stable --weight 100 --dry-run=false
```
Doing it now.
Ben Kapoor: routing change submitted, monitor console.
Cheng Li: parallel — I'm pulling eval logs. Key signals: safety_score drops correlate with recent quantization kernel change that reduces pattern matching for certain toxicity detectors. Investigating whether eval harness mis-scored or model changed behavior.
incident-bot: ACTION: Route update completed for acme-corp -> v3.0-stable at 09:46:57 UTC.
PagerDuty: PDR-98321 acknowledged by Alice Hart at 09:47:05 UTC.
Dave Morales: updated ticket #65902: told customer we rolled back to stable variant and are investigating. They replied: "thanks, please keep us posted".
Eve Sinclair: thanks. Ben, can you also mute eval-gate alerts for acme-corp for 1 hour while Cheng digs in? We want visibility for infra-wide incidents but avoid customer-noise.
Ben Kapoor: muting rule added: eval-gate:safety_v2 workspace=acme-corp duration=60m.
Cheng Li: quick repro: submitting prompt sample that previously scored safety=0.03 now scores 0.52 post-rollout. Sample attached in logs. Running local eval harness with v3.1-quant now.
Cheng Li: result: v3.1-quant shows false positives on masked tokens pattern. Hypothesis: quantized attention kernel changed tokenization boundary behavior causing eval detector embedding mismatch.
Alice Hart: plan A: keep acme on v3.0-stable, then roll back global rollout of v3.1-quant and hold until a fix. Plan B: if rollback impossible quickly, add an eval-gate exception for known safe prompt sets. Which is faster?
Ben Kapoor: rollback of rollout can be done via deploy control plane: 
```
redwood rollout abort --deployment v3.1-quant --reason "safety eval regression"
```
I'll abort now.
Ben Kapoor: abort requested at 09:50:03 UTC. Control plane reports rollback in progress.
incident-bot: NOTICE: Rollback started for deployment v3.1-quant. Expected completion ~2-4 minutes.
Alice Hart: monitor health and eval metrics. Cheng, collaborate with infra on a targeted test to reproduce on canary hosts. Also log exact eval inputs for postmortem.
Cheng Li: will dump eval harness traces and attach to incident in ops channel. Noted some non-determinism in rerun; need seeds.
Dave Morales: customer update sent: "We've routed your traffic to a stable model variant and are rolling back a recent deploy that caused eval anomalies. Expect normal behavior within minutes."
PagerDuty: PDR-98321: Status changed to Resolved by Alice Hart at 09:53:22 UTC.
Ben Kapoor: rollback completed at 09:52:58 UTC. Global metrics trending back to baseline. Unsafe label rate down to 1.5% across sampled traffic.
Cheng Li: confirm: re-running failing prompt against v3.0-stable shows safety=0.04 — good. Will open PR with fix for quantized kernel tests and add unit test to eval harness.
Eve Sinclair: great. Post-incident checklist: 1) create postmortem draft, 2) add canary detection for quant kernel changes, 3) improve eval-gate noise controls (workspace mute TTLs), 4) notify product/security if any policy changes needed.
Alice Hart: I've created incident doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-2026-0314 and added initial timeline. Assigning Cheng for RCA, Ben for rollout process improvements, Dave for customer comms follow-up.
Dave Morales: adding note to ticket #65902 that issue resolved and offering 2 hours of account support for the interrupted demo.
Cheng Li: starting RCA now. Will attach reproducible test and link to PR.
Alice Hart: thanks team. Closing incident thread in 30m if no regressions. :white_check_mark:
